aspectTitle: Live-region politeness is semantically wrong for the message's urgency and update frequency
aspectDescription: The status message IS in a working, present live region and IS announced, so every automated tool and every seed (which all model the crude 'no live region at all' failure) passes it. The defect is that the chosen politeness is semantically wrong for what the message MEANS and how often it fires. Two opposite failure shapes: (a) a low-value, high-frequency message (a ticking stock/crypto price, a per-keystroke 'N results' count, a 'last saved 3s ago' autosave heartbeat, a 'people viewing this item: 14' badge) is wired role=alert / aria-live=assertive, so it rudely interrupts and clobbers whate
scenario: E-commerce running-shoe store with an instant search filter: a 'N results' counter beneath the search box updates on every keystroke. The counter is a present, valid live region wired role=alert (assertive), so typing 'shoes' fires five assertive announcements in under a second, each interrupting and clobbering the last. A low-value, high-frequency count should be polite (role=status), not assertive.
mechanism: role=alert maps to an assertive live region: each text change interrupts current speech. The region's text is replaced on every 'input' event, so a per-keystroke result count repeatedly preempts whatever the screen reader was reading and cuts off its own prior announcements. The message is announced (absence-checkers pass) but at a politeness inappropriate for its low value and high cadence — the 'too chatty' failure.

For a screen-reader user reading the article, the price tape assertively interrupts the narration every two seconds, indefinitely. The user can never finish reading a paragraph because the AT keeps cutting in to recite fluctuating prices. The markup is valid; the defect is the wrong politeness for the message's value and cadence.

scenario: Government unemployment-benefits wizard, 'certify your claim' step. The user must read a long legal certification statement before checking the agree box. A secure-session region (present, valid) is wired aria-live=polite; when the 30-second expiry countdown is injected, polite politeness queues it behind the long statement the screen reader is still narrating, so it is heard only after the session has already ended and the answers are discarded. A blocking, time-critical countdown must be assertive.

scenario: Higher-ed LMS essay editor with an autosave indicator in the toolbar. The indicator is a present, valid live region wired role=alert (assertive); a debounced handler flips it 'Saving…' -> 'All changes saved' roughly every two seconds while the student is still typing. Each flip assertively interrupts the screen reader's typing echo, so the student stops hearing their own words. An autosave confirmation is low-value and belongs in a polite region at most.

The information is low-value, high-cadence — it should be polite (role=status). Valid markup, wrong politeness.

aspectTitle: Partial update without aria-atomic announces only the changed fragment, losing meaning
aspectDescription: A persistent status region is correctly marked (role=status / aria-live=polite) and DOES announce on change — passing every tool and every seed. But only an inner sub-node holding the volatile value is updated, and the region is not atomic, so the screen reader speaks just the bare changed token in isolation: 'three' instead of 'three items in cart', 'red' instead of 'filtered to red, 24 products', '2' instead of '2 errors on this page', '85' instead of '85 percent complete'. The visible string is perfectly meaningful because the sighted user sees the surrounding static label; the announced fr
scenario: Coffee storefront header cart 'X items in cart' wrapped in role=status; clicking Add to cart rewrites ONLY the inner <span id=cart-count> 0->3 while the region has no aria-atomic, so AT announces a bare 'three' instead of 'three items in cart'.
mechanism: role=status is polite and spec-atomic by default, but ARIA22 warns this default is not honored in some AT environments; with aria-atomic unset and only the inner count node mutated, AT speaks just the changed token ('three'), losing the static 'items in cart' framing that carries the meaning.

aspectTitle: Role/aria-live added together with (or after) the content, instead of pre-existing empty
aspectDescription: The FINAL DOM looks perfect: there is a <div role="status" aria-live="polite"> containing the message, with valid markup. A static scan and the seeds (which key on absence of role/aria-live) both pass it. But the region — or its role/aria-live attribute — was created/attached at the same moment the message text was injected, rather than existing as an empty container at page load. Most screen readers only announce mutations to live regions that were already present and registered, so a region born with its content never fires. F103 calls out this timing limb explicitly; ARIA19 requires the emp
scenario:
City recycling-bin request form: on submit the handler does resultArea.innerHTML = '
Your recycling cart request was received…
', so the role=status attribute is born inside the same markup string as the confirmation text. The resting DOM is a textbook-correct live region but no live region existed at page load.
mechanism: F103 timing limb / ARIA19 step 1: a live region must be present-and-empty when the AT registers it so a later content mutation fires. Here the role=status node and its text enter the DOM together via innerHTML, producing no empty-region-then-mutation transition, so NVDA/JAWS/VoiceOver stay silent; the screen-reader user gets no submit confirmation (and the form was hidden).

aspectTitle: Announced text lacks the visual context that makes it meaningful (no offscreen text for AT)
aspectDescription: The status is announced cleanly and the whole atomic string is read — so tools and seeds pass. The failure is that the VISIBLE text relies on spatial/visual proximity for meaning, and no offscreen/extra text was added to the live region to supply that context to a non-sighted user. The Understanding's canonical example: a bare '3' appears next to a shopping-cart icon — sighted users understand 'cart: 3', AT users hear an orphaned '3'. Likewise a green checkmark + 'Done' next to a specific row, or 'Saved' with no album name where the visible popup sits over the 'Wedding' album. The remediation
scenario: E-commerce hiking-gear store: a valid role=status/aria-live=polite/aria-atomic=true cart badge updates from 0 to 1/2/3 on Add-to-Cart, announcing only the bare number. The word 'cart' that gives the number meaning lives on the adjacent icon glyph's aria-label (so 1.1.1 passes) but sits outside the atomic region and is never re-read on update.
mechanism: On update the polite live region announces its entire atomic contents — just the digit ('three'). It does not re-read the sibling glyph's 'Shopping cart' aria-label, because a polite live announcement speaks the changed region's atomic contents, not adjacent unchanged nodes. AT hears an orphaned number; remediation per the Understanding is offscreen 'in shopping cart' text or placing the cart image with alt INSIDE the atomic region (ARIA22).

Fix: include the symbol inside each atomic region.

aspectTitle: Non-textual status (icon/sound) given a status role but no usable text alternative
aspectDescription: A status is conveyed purely by a non-text change — a spinner->checkmark icon swap, a red 'x' badge, a color/shape change, or an audio chime — and the author DID wrap it in a live region (role=status/alert), so the absence-of-role checkers and the seeds pass. The failure is that the icon carries empty/decorative/absent alt (alt='', aria-hidden, a CSS background image with no text, an SVG with no accessible name) or the sound has no visual+text equivalent, so the live region fires but announces nothing, or announces a filename, or announces a meaningless symbol. The SC routes this through 1.1.1:
scenario: Insurance auto-quote wizard (step 2 of 5). Inline licence-number validation swaps a neutral gray dot to a red 'X' SVG inside a present role="alert" region on invalid submit. The alert fires but its only child is an aria-hidden SVG with no text, so it announces an empty string.
mechanism: role="alert" container is present at load and its mutation fires the live-region boundary, but the injected red-X SVG carries aria-hidden="true" with no <title>/aria-label and there is no sibling text node, so the region's computed text content is the empty string — the screen reader announces 'alert' then silence while a sighted user sees an unmistakable error X. Headless check confirmed announced text == "" with the red-X path present.

aspectTitle: Mis-scoping the status-message boundary: change-of-context exceptions vs. genuine in-scope status
aspectDescription: This aspect tests the threshold judgment that precedes every other limb: does the dynamic change even MEET the definition of a status message (success/result, waiting, progress, or error AND not delivered via a change of context)? Two failure directions, both requiring semantic judgment: (a) FALSE POSITIVE pressure — content that the Understanding explicitly EXCEPTS is treated as needing a live region or, worse, is force-fed into role=alert and over-announces: an error shown in a focus-taking dialog (already a change of context, governed elsewhere), expand/collapse of a menu/accordion/tab (gov
scenario: Halcyon Credit Union wire-transfer form. On submit failure (routing number belongs to a closed institution) the page opens a real modal dialog (role=dialog, aria-modal=true) that moves focus into itself, traps Tab, and supports Esc. The error text lives entirely inside the dialog; there is deliberately no role=status/aria-live anywhere. Canonical excepted case: error delivered via a focus-taking dialog is a change of context, so it does not meet the status-message definition and 4.1.3 is N/A.
mechanism: The submit handler calls focus() into the modal, so the change is announced as a dialog (change of context). Per the Understanding's 'Examples of changes that are not status messages', an error in a focus-taking dialog is excepted from 4.1.3; the absence of a live region is correct, not a defect. The only candidate message is delivered by change of context, so the SC does not apply.
